tasks.title: HANGS Construction Services · Q3 2026 Quarterly Review
tasks.description: Review HANGS Construction Services LLC's quarter ended September 30, 2026 for the bonding company and the lender from 8 Excel, PDF and Word files: the comparative trial balance, the interim statements and budget, the controller's written answers, the job schedule, the Q3 payroll ledger and the bank's loan statement and covenants. Inquiry and analytical procedures, not an audit: compare the quarter, investigate every change over the threshold, corroborate each answer, rebuild revenue from the jobs, set expectations for wages and interest and recompute the loan covenants. Produce formula-linked workpapers with tickmarks and a draft review memo. The CPA reviews, decides every open item and concludes; the machine expresses no conclusion.

propertyEvents.result: Explain the billing swing and recompute the retainage
propertyEvents.locator: Sep 30 2026!A8:O16 and Jun 30 2026!A8:O15; contract, estimate, cost, earned revenue and billings by job

propertyEvents.result: The schedule’s underbillings $390,950.00 and overbillings $341,000.00 are the books’ at both dates. The quarter billed $20,732,500.00 against $21,696,700.00 of revenue: the $964,200.00 difference is the swing exactly. Alder Point alone moved $612,950.00, from $337,500.00 overbilled to $275,450.00 underbilled, as Q2 says. Retainage receivable $2,197,750.00 is 5% of $43,955,000.00 billed to date.

propertyEvents.result: Test each job’s margin for the quarter against its June 30 estimate
propertyEvents.locator: Sep 30 2026!A8:O16 and Jun 30 2026!A8:O15; contract, estimate, cost, earned revenue and billings by job

propertyEvents.result: At June 30 margins the quarter’s jobs would have earned $2,180,047.50 of gross profit; they earned $1,797,327.50. One job explains it: Tideflats Cold Storage earned $82,800.00 on $4,048,000.00 of revenue, $382,720.00 below its June margin, because its estimate rose from $16,284,000.00 to $17,480,000.00 and the whole year-to-date effect lands in this quarter. That is the revision Q3 describes. The job still expects a 5.0% margin, so no loss provision is needed; the backcharge claim is rightly not recorded (JOB-01).
propertyEvents.locator: Sep 30 2026!A8:O16 and Jun 30 2026!A8:O15; contract, estimate, cost, earned revenue and billings by job

propertyEvents.result: Test the change order the schedule counts before the owner has signed it
propertyEvents.locator: Sep 30 2026!A8:O16 and Jun 30 2026!A8:O15; contract, estimate, cost, earned revenue and billings by job

propertyEvents.result: Alder Point’s total contract includes pending change order PCO-14, $640,000.00, which the owner has not signed (Q2). At 40.5% complete it puts $259,200.00 into this quarter’s revenue and gross profit, more than materiality. Whether an unsigned change order can be counted yet is a judgment under the revenue standard’s limit on uncertain amounts; the CPA reads the pricing and the architect’s review (REV-01). Without it Alder Point would be $16,250.00 against its billings.
propertyEvents.locator: Sep 30 2026!A8:O16 and Jun 30 2026!A8:O15; contract, estimate, cost, earned revenue and billings by job

propertyEvents.result: Revenue and costs tie to the jobs · the $964,200 swing explained · Tideflats $382,720 below its June margin · PCO-14 $259,200 unsigned

propertyEvents.result: Set an expectation for interest from each loan’s balance, rate and days, and compare it with the books
propertyEvents.locator: PDF page 1; term loan and line of credit activity, balances and the interest accrued for September

propertyEvents.result: From the balances, the rates and actual/360 days the quarter’s interest should be $98,140.50; the books show $91,455.50. The books’ figure is exactly what the bank debited on July 1, August 1 and September 1, the interest for June, July and August: interest is recorded when paid. September’s $35,350.00, on the bank’s own statement, is not accrued (accrued interest in the books: $0.00), and June’s $28,665.00 landed in this quarter. Expense is understated $6,685.00 and liabilities $35,350.00 (INT-01). This contradicts Q5, which says interest is accrued monthly (INQ-01).
propertyEvents.locator: PDF page 1; term loan and line of credit activity, balances and the interest accrued for September

propertyEvents.result: Recompute the three loan covenants as the agreement defines them
propertyEvents.locator: PDF page 1; section 7 financial covenants, interest terms and definitions

propertyEvents.result: Working capital $4,789,499.00 (minimum $3,000,000) and total liabilities to tangible net worth 2.46 to 1 (maximum 2.75) are met. Tangible net worth must leave out everything due from affiliates: Juniper Ridge Partners’ $571,000.00 receivable, $94,000.00 retainage and $50,500.00 underbilled, $715,500.00 in all. That leaves $6,629,999.00, $129,999.00 above the $6,500,000 minimum. Record INT-01 and leave out PCO-14 and it falls to $6,335,449.00, $164,551.00 short: the covenant, and whether the loans stay long-term, turn on the CPA’s judgment on PCO-14 (COV-01).
propertyEvents.locator: PDF page 1; section 7 financial covenants, interest terms and definitions
propertyEvents.tapeTitle: Tangible Net Worth, as the Agreement Defines It

tape.label: Less Due From Juniper Ridge Partners, an Affiliate
Less PCO-14, If Not Yet Counted

propertyEvents.result: Wages tie to payroll · interest recorded when paid, $35,350 not accrued · covenants met with $129,999 of net worth headroom
Ready for the CPA
Add up what was found and set it against materiality

Known misstatements add up to $6,685.00 of expense, 6.7% of the $100,000.00 interim review materiality, with $35,350.00 of accrued interest missing from liabilities (INT-01). The judgment that matters is larger: PCO-14 puts $259,200.00 into revenue before the owner has signed, 259% of materiality, and decides the net worth covenant (REV-01, COV-01). The statements also need a related party note for Juniper Ridge Partners (RP-01). Concluding is the CPA’s job; the machine stops here.

events.result: From the balances, the rates and actual/360 days the quarter’s interest should be $98,140.50; the books show $91,455.50. The books’ figure is exactly what the bank debited on July 1, August 1 and September 1, the interest for June, July and August: interest is recorded when paid. September’s $35,350.00, on the bank’s own statement, is not accrued (accrued interest in the books: $0.00), and June’s $28,665.00 landed in this quarter. Expense is understated $6,685.00 and liabilities $35,350.00 (INT-01). This contradicts Q5, which says interest is accrued monthly (INQ-01).

events.result: Working capital $4,789,499.00 (minimum $3,000,000) and total liabilities to tangible net worth 2.46 to 1 (maximum 2.75) are met. Tangible net worth must leave out everything due from affiliates: Juniper Ridge Partners’ $571,000.00 receivable, $94,000.00 retainage and $50,500.00 underbilled, $715,500.00 in all. That leaves $6,629,999.00, $129,999.00 above the $6,500,000 minimum. Record INT-01 and leave out PCO-14 and it falls to $6,335,449.00, $164,551.00 short: the covenant, and whether the loans stay long-term, turn on the CPA’s judgment on PCO-14 (COV-01).

events.result: Wages tie to payroll · interest recorded when paid, $35,350 not accrued · covenants met with $129,999 of net worth headroom
Ready for the CPA
Add up what was found and set it against materiality

Known misstatements add up to $6,685.00 of expense, 6.7% of the $100,000.00 interim review materiality, with $35,350.00 of accrued interest missing from liabilities (INT-01). The judgment that matters is larger: PCO-14 puts $259,200.00 into revenue before the owner has signed, 259% of materiality, and decides the net worth covenant (REV-01, COV-01). The statements also need a related party note for Juniper Ridge Partners (RP-01). Concluding is the CPA’s job; the machine stops here.
